title: A Content-Security-Policy is served
rationale: The strongest browser defence against injected script.
hint: Define the CSP in netlify.toml or the host's header config. A project that serves only an HTTP API declares "surface": "api" in baseline.json and gets HOS-009..012 instead.

title: HSTS is enabled
rationale: Forces HTTPS and prevents downgrade attacks.

title: Framing and MIME sniffing are blocked
script-src has no unsafe-inline
rationale: 'unsafe-inline' in script-src voids the CSP against XSS.

title: Required environment is documented
rationale: A .env.example lists every variable without values.

title: Hashed assets are cached immutably
rationale: Fast repeat visits cost nothing and need no revalidation.

title: No secret is exposed to the client bundle
rationale: Anything prefixed VITE_ ends up in the browser.

title: Every deploy can be rolled back
rationale: Immutable deploys with one-click rollback turn incidents into minutes.

title: API responses carry a deny-all Content-Security-Policy
rationale: An API cannot promise it never returns HTML: a framework error page or a reflected value with the wrong Content-Type is rendered by the browser. default-src 'none' gives such a response nothing to load or run; frame-ancestors 'none' stops it being framed, and it does not fall back to default-src.
hint: Send Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none' on every response from one place: a middleware (Azure Functions IFunctionsWorkerMiddleware, ASP.NET Core app.Use, a Node header hook, helmet with defaultSrc and frameAncestors 'none') or customHeaders in the Azure Functions host.json. See the OWASP REST Security Cheat Sheet.

title: API responses forbid MIME sniffing
rationale: Without nosniff a browser may read a JSON or text response as HTML or script and run what an attacker put into it.
hint: Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff from the same middleware or host.json customHeaders as HOS-009; helmet sets it by default.

title: API responses are not stored by caches
rationale: API responses carry per-request and often personal data, and a browser or shared cache must not hand them to the next reader. Immutable caching (HOS-006) is for hashed static assets, which an API does not serve.
hint: Send Cache-Control: no-store from the same middleware or host.json customHeaders as HOS-009; relax it per endpoint only for public, non-personal data.

title: API responses enable HSTS
rationale: A platform's HTTPS-only redirect protects the server, but every request a client starts over plain HTTP has already travelled in clear with its credentials. HSTS makes browsers refuse plain HTTP to the API for its max-age.
hint: Send Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains (or enable hsts in the Azure Functions host.json, UseHsts in ASP.NET Core, helmet in Node) and keep the platform's HTTPS-only switch on.
